title: Projection pushdown — Selective Field Retrieval
description:
Selective field retrieval answers a projection, not a whole record: the caller names the fields it needs and the store returns just those, skipping the rest. Over a near-boundless archive this cuts transferred bytes by orders of magnitude, speeds up mobile clients, and reduces exposure of fields the caller never asked for. The technique combines a declared field schema, push-down projection at the storage layer, and a strict contract that unrequested fields are never serialized.

This record documents the projection pushdown approach: Push the field list into the storage engine so unrequested columns are never read from disk, not merely dropped before serialization.
